finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and persists it, so any logged-in user can set privileged fields such as role, isAdmin, tenantId or id on their own account (privilege escalation / tenant hopping).
finding.source: req.body JSON of PUT /me, sent by any authenticated user

trace.note: Object.assign merges all body keys into req.user
req.store.save persists the modified user, including privileged fields
Full user object is returned in the response

finding.guards_checked: Reviewed the only file in the directory. No allowlist, schema validation, or field filtering exists in this handler. Authentication middleware that sets req.user is not present here and was not visible; even if present, it only authenticates the caller and does not limit which fields are writable. The sibling route /me/profile (line 10) shows the intended pattern: it destructures displayName and bio only, so it is safe. Object.assign does not set __proto__ on the target through a JSON-parsed own key in a way that pollutes Object.prototype, so prototype pollution was not reported.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 does Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist, users.js:6 saves it, and users.js:7 returns it, so any authenticated user can write role, isAdmin or tenantId; the only control, in the safe sibling route at users.js:11, is not applied here.
